 Couple Has No Savings And Owes Over $428K, Yet Spends $1,029 A Month On Pets. Ramit Sethi Says, ‘Your Dog Doesn’t Deserve It’
 Young woman and cute Australian Shepherd dog with empty bowl at home (Credit: Pets-Photo via Shutterstock) Casey B. Renner Sat, November 14, 2026 at 6:00 PM CST 6 min read Benzinga and Yahoo Finance LLC may earn commission or revenue on some items through the links below. 
 A married couple owed more than $428,000 and had nothing in savings. They were having trouble paying rent on time and still budgeted $1,029 a month for their two dogs. 
 When Addison and James went through their expenses with personal finance author Ramit Sethi on his "Money for Couples" podcast, that was one bill he wanted them to rethink. "Your dog doesn't deserve it," he told them.

 Payday Would Fix It. Until It Didn't. 
 Addison struggled to get James to talk about money and felt she was putting her own career on hold to keep the household running. She asked Sethi for help and told him how serious things had gotten. "We will likely divorce if things continue on as they have," she wrote. 
 James said he kept making promises to Addison because he thought more money would come in. 
 The couple went through their debts with Sethi. Of the $428,263 they listed, about $350,000 was in student loans. They also estimated they owed $25,000 on personal loans and $15,000 on credit cards. James said he owed about $40,000 in back taxes. 
 One More Bag Of Dog Food 
 After their first dog died of cancer, Addison wanted to adopt his father. He was older, and she said no one else wanted him. 
 Trending: Think Your IRA Can Only Hold Stocks And Funds? Think Again. Here's What A Self-Directed IRA Can Actually Invest In. 
 James wasn't sure they could afford another dog. The adoption was free, and Addison figured they would spend a little more on food and pay for a checkup every so often. "We didn't crunch any numbers," she said. 
 She ended up spending $6,000, more than she expected. James found out how much she'd spent once the dog was home. 
 The couple budgeted $1,029 a month for their dogs. Then one of the dogs got sick, and the vet bill alone came to $1,500. Sethi also spotted several Chewy orders on their statement. Altogether, they spent $2,667 on the dogs that month. 
 An unexpected bill can make it harder to decide how much to save while paying down debt. People weighing those priorities can take a short quiz through Finance Advisors to get matched with up to three financial professionals. 
 See Also: There's More Than One Way To Put Cash To Work. Some Accredited Investors Are Looking Beyond Savings Accounts. 
 Story Continues The Dogs Kept Their Treats 
 James thought $250 a month would cover food and training treats for both dogs. He also wanted to put money aside for vet bills, so Sethi asked which he would fund first, retirement or the dogs' care. 
 "Can we do both?" James asked. 
 The couple settled on $400 a month for vet bills and agreed to hold off on unnecessary purchases until they saved $10,000. With the spending cuts and the extra pay Addison expected from returning to full-time work, they projected that fixed costs would drop from 154% of their take-home pay to 63%. 
 A month later, they said they had stopped eating out and buying convenience-store snacks. They were planning meals at home and sitting down together once a week to go over their spending. 
 "Now, we've cut a lot, but we're still alive and kicking," Addison said.

 Building Wealth Across More Than Just The Market 
 Building a resilient portfolio means thinking beyond a single asset or market trend. Economic cycles shift, sectors rise and fall, and no one investment performs well in every environment. That's why many investors look to diversify with platforms that provide access to real estate, fixed-income opportunities, precious metals, and even self-directed retirement accounts. By spreading exposure across multiple asset classes, it becomes easier to manage risk, capture steady returns, and create long-term wealth that isn't tied to the fortunes of just one company or industry. 
 EquityMultiple 
 For accredited investors looking beyond stocks and bonds, EquityMultiple provides access to vetted commercial real estate deals starting at $5,000 , with only ~5% of opportunities passing their due diligence process. 
 Arrived 
 Backed by Jeff Bezos, Arrived Homes makes real estate investing accessible with a low barrier to entry. Investors can buy fractional shares of single-family rentals and vacation homes starting with as little as $100 . This allows everyday investors to diversify into real estate, collect rental income, and build long-term wealth without needing to manage properties directly. 
 American PowerGen 
 As artificial intelligence drives a surge in electricity demand, reliable power generation is becoming a critical part of the technology ecosystem. American PowerGen is developing natural gas-fired power plants in Texas, a fast-growing market fueled by AI data centers, manufacturing expansion, and population growth. By advancing projects through permitting, fuel supply, and grid interconnection, the company is positioning itself to help meet rising energy needs while offering investors exposure to the infrastructure supporting the next wave of AI and industrial growth. 
 Bito 
 As AI coding tools take on more of the work traditionally done by developers, companies are facing new challenges around code quality, context and the rising cost of AI-powered development. Bito is building software designed to help AI coding agents better understand complex codebases while helping companies control AI development costs. Founded by former PubMatic executives, Bito has raised more than $10 million from institutional and individual investors and is now raising additional capital through a Wefunder offering, giving investors an opportunity to invest in a company targeting an emerging need within the rapidly expanding AI software market. 
 FarmTogether 
 Farmland has historically held its value through market volatility and delivered returns uncorrelated to stocks and bonds. For accredited investors, FarmTogether offers direct access to high-quality U.S. farmland starting at $15,000 — fully managed, with no landlord headaches. 
 Fundrise 
 Private real estate and private credit can add income and stability to a stock-heavy portfolio. Fundrise offers access to diversified private real estate and credit strategies through an easy-to-use platform, with professionally managed portfolios designed to generate passive income and long-term growth.
